learning_outcomes.text: Has basic knowledge of concepts related to electromagnetic compatibility and electric power quality, electromagnetic disturbances, principles of standardization and measurement assessment of voltage quality.
Has knowledge of the classification of voltage RMS disturbances, slow and rapid voltage changes.
Has knowledge of voltage and current distortion: harmonic and interharmonic in the band up to 2.5 kHz and emission of high-frequency disturbances in converter systems.
Has basic knowledge of the cooperation of power electronic systems with the supply network.
Has basic knowledge of voltage sags and swells and short interruptions in power supply.
Has basic knowledge of voltage and current asymmetry.
Has basic knowledge of reactive power compensation and capacitor operation in an environment of distorted voltages and currents.
Has basic knowledge of the cooperation of distributed energy sources with the power system.
Has basic knowledge of uninterruptible power supplies and the costs of poor energy quality.
Can assess the quality of electricity supply based on single-point measurements.
Can analyze and formulate conclusions regarding the causes of poor electricity supply quality and propose technical measures to eliminate the effects of poor voltage quality.
Can prepare documentation for an engineering task and prepare a text containing a discussion of the results of this task.
Can work individually and in a team; can estimate the time needed to complete an assigned task; can develop and implement a work schedule ensuring deadlines are met.
Is aware of responsibility for their own work and readiness to adhere to team work principles and take responsibility for jointly implemented tasks.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to electromagnetic compatibility, classification of electromagnetic disturbances, basic definitions, standardization principles, basics of primary assessment of electricity supply quality.
Classification of RMS voltage disturbances, slow voltage changes (sources, numerical description and measurement principles, effects, voltage stabilization methods); rapid voltage changes.

Voltage fluctuations - sources, effects, numerical description and measurement principles, methods of fluctuation elimination, localization of fluctuation sources, propagation of fluctuations in the power system, summation of voltage fluctuations.

Voltage and current distortion - power theories in circuits with distorted waveforms, sources, effects, numerical description and measurement principles, elimination methods, source localization, propagation of harmonics in the power system, passive and active filtration, interharmonics.
Interaction of converter systems with the supply network, power electronic interfaces of distributed energy sources and loads.

Voltage sags - sources, effects, numerical description and measurement principles, elimination methods, source localization, propagation of harmonics in the power system, DVR system, electricity supply contract.
Asymmetry of voltages and currents - sources, effects, numerical description and measurement principles, elimination methods, source localization, propagation of asymmetry in the power system.
Capacitor as an element of the power system - reactive power compensation and filtration systems.
High-frequency disturbances in power electronic systems.
Distributed energy sources and voltage quality.
Energy quality and the electricity market.
Uninterruptible power supply systems, energy storage.
Reactive power compensation in the presence of non-linear loads.
Voltage drops and voltage fluctuations in networks.
Single-point measurements of voltage quality indicators.
Measurements of electricity supply quality indicators.
assessment_rules: Lectures are credited based on a positive test result. Laboratory classes are credited based on performing the laboratory exercises and a positive grade from all colloquiums. A positive assessment of all laboratory classes is required to pass the module.
